title: Resolve Java var types through cross-file receiver method calls
wanted_capability: Authoritative Java var type resolution for cross-file receiver method calls via a JDTLS-backed seam: methodRegions (facts) emits resolved_type for syntactically-derivable cases and null for cross-file/LSP-dependent cases; an analysis.resolveVarTypes reduction (or lsp.typeAt/hover follow-up) fills the nulls by querying a harness-owned JDTLS session. The facts module itself must NOT reach cross-file/LSP (charter).
missing_primitive: jdtls-seam: bro-lsp Language::Java (JDTLS session pool) + a new lsp.typeAt/lsp.hover harness binding verb + an analysis.resolveVarTypes({file, spans}) reduction that calls the pool
fallback_used: Probe agent manually searched for the callee declaration and copied the declared return type into explicit helper parameters.
notes:
REFRAMED (2026-06-18) to the JDTLS-backed implementation path. Original framing ("methodRegions should provide resolved_type for cross-file receiver method calls") is architecturally blocked: resolve_var_declaration_type lives in scope.rs, part of the bbox-refactor facts module, which is pure-bytes by charter (no LSP, no daemon state, no cross-file). It cannot reach cross-file declarations by construction.

Solve = a harness-owned JDTLS seam (mirrors the existing rust-analyzer lsp.rename pattern in crates/bro-harness/src/bindings/lsp_facts.rs): (1) extend bro-lsp with Language::Java + JDTLS binary config + a JDTLS readiness handshake; (2) add an lsp.typeAt/lsp.hover verb (textDocument/hover) returning the resolved type at a hash-anchored span — the harness already does byte<->UTF-16 conversion and hash-anchored spans; (3) an analysis.resolveVarTypes({file, spans}) reduction that warms the JDTLS pool and returns authoritative types. JDTLS textDocument/hover at the var declarator resolves the cross-file receiver method return definitively because JDTLS indexes the whole project. methodRegions (facts) stays the fast syntactic first pass; unresolved vars get authoritative types via the seam.

This supersedes the index-backed recommendation in thread-8d968b2d Note 26: the corpus index is (a) unreachable from cells by decision af3c4783 (zero daemon reach-back), (b) name-level only — cannot resolve cross-file receiver return types authoritatively, and (c) symbol vertices aren't even searchable yet (gap-496fe07f). The seam keeps the container test passing (harness owns the JDTLS session, warm-pooled, fail-closed RX-V3). Caveat: JDTLS needs the Gradle/Maven project model, so the seam is real-worktree-viable (where the campaign runs) but not fixture-viable for the standalone isolate CLI — facts remain the fixture path.
